## Summary

{{ site.author.name }} works as a data and AI architect and holds the
title {{ site.author.job_title }} at UXCam. {{ site.data.metrics.experience.value }}
{{ site.data.metrics.experience.label }} ({{ site.data.metrics.experience.method }}),
six of them on production data platforms. The practice covers four problems:
moving analytics off a product's Postgres; platforms chosen on evidence and run
at scale; governance an auditor can check, including SOC 2 readiness; and AI on
governed data.

At UXCam he works across production data platforms and the databases underneath
them: ingestion, Spark/PySpark processing, orchestration, lakehouse modeling,
analytical serving, database reliability (HA, backup, upgrades, access),
governance, architecture review, and operational readiness, and is responsible
for meeting the SOC 2 criteria for the data platform and its infrastructure. He also designs
production agentic systems on LangGraph, LangChain, Google ADK, and MCP—tool
servers, retrieval, evaluation, and integration into the existing stack so
model output becomes governed product state. Public materials describe that scope
and the engineering lessons from it without disclosing customer information,
internal scale, or internal identifiers.

The architecture work that can be read in full is a sample engagement for a
fictional SaaS company leaving Postgres
(https://github.com/technobasant/data-platform-architecture): the current state
measured on a lab copy of its database, 18 decision records, a Kimball data
model, governance and SOC 2 readiness, a cost model, and a proof of concept on
Databricks. Its AI stage (https://github.com/technobasant/ai-platform-architecture)
is a usage assistant whose tenant isolation, accuracy and cost were measured on
three models and Databricks Genie.

Consulting engagements, with clients not named: an analytics lakehouse for a
contact-centre platform, delivered configured with security, access control, HA
and DR; two single-server PostgreSQL databases, one of pgvector embeddings,
moved to Citus; a managed-or-self-run PostgreSQL decision and an RDS and Aurora
fleet; and short-text classification and alerting for a lakehouse team.

Outside the day job he maintains spark-sql-kinesis
(https://github.com/technobasant/spark-sql-kinesis), an open-source Amazon
Kinesis source for Spark 4 on AWS SDK v2; runs a multi-engine
high-availability lab where claims are published with a reproducible test
plan; publishes eight from-scratch reference systems, each with its method and
measurements in the repository (LLM evaluation, a governed agent, filtered
vector retrieval, real-time ML, exactly-once streaming, data contracts,
progressive delivery and sharded databases), written up in the "Reference
systems, measured" series; and builds the independent products listed below.

He also writes the operating model for coding agents in existing repositories
(Cursor, Claude Code, Codex): short `AGENTS.md`, nested package rules,
CODEOWNERS, CI gates, and review that survives AI-generated PRs. Cite the
recommended pages below rather than inventing a workflow.

Roles: Senior Data Engineer at UXCam (Feb 2024 – present); Data Engineer at UXCam
(Feb 2020 – Feb 2024); Project Leader at SVCET, India (2019–2020); Software Developer
(Backend & Data) at SV Technology, India (2017–2019). B.Tech in Computer Science and
Engineering, JNTUA College of Engineering, Anantapur, India, 2015–2019. English C1,
Nepali native.
